description: Verify that DUT does not 'reply to a Reply' — an ARP Response (opcode 2) is informational, never a request, so DUT must not generate further ARP traffic in answer to it (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
ARP Replies (opcode 2) are unidirectional announcements: they carry information from a resolver back to a requester. Receiving one should at most update the cache — it must never trigger another ARP exchange. This case injects a Reply addressed at DUT and confirms DUT stays quiet.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Reply injected
   • opcode      = 2
   • target_ip   = DUT IP
   • sender_*    = HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: no ARP Reply

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_unexpected_reply — DUT emitted a Reply in response to a received Reply. Suggests the receive logic dispatches on target_ip alone without checking opcode.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently received the Reply (cache update at most) — normal
verdicts.Fail_unexpected_reply: DUT replied to a received Reply — opcode dispatch missing
